title: Factors of a monomial in a complete saturated monoid local model
statement: Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and suppose it is sharp, meaning that $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. For a coefficient ring $L$, write $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the ring of finite sums of symbols $c z^q t^e$, with $q\in P$, $e\in\mathbf N^n$, $c\in L$, and multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. If $L$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $R$ be one of the following rings: (i) $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$; (ii) $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ for a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In case (ii), $p$ is prime and the residue field of $C$ is arbitrary of characteristic $p$. Write $z^q\in R$ for the image of the indicated monomial. For every $q\in P$ and $b,c\in R$ with $bc=z^q$, there are $r\in P$ and a unit $u\in R^\times$ such that $b=u z^r$. This includes $q=0$, $P=\{0\}$ and $n=0$.

proof.text: Let $S=\{z^a:a\in P\}$ and let $\ell:R\to S^{-1}R$ be localization at these monomials (fractions and their equivalence are as defined in the cited interface). From $bc=z^q$ we compute in $S^{-1}R$ that $\ell(b)\,\bigl(\ell(c)/\ell(z^q)\bigr)=\ell(bc)/\ell(z^q)=1$. The ring is commutative, so this is a two-sided inverse of $\ell(b)$. Hence $b$ belongs to the inverse image of the unit group. This calculation requires neither normality nor a divisor-class computation.

source.place: VI 1.4 and 1.6, printed pp. 69--70, motivate the recognition interface; the explicit inverse calculation is by Q39.

proof.text: Apply the complete-local recognition equality [lem-trf-complete-toric-kato-recognition] to $P,n,R$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given finite generation, integrality, saturation and sharpness of $P$, and either the field coefficient model or the stated Cohen quotient with $\theta-p$ in the indicated monomial-and-parameter ideal. By step 1, $b\in\ell^{-1}((S^{-1}R)^\times)$. The right side of the equality therefore supplies $r\in P$ and $u\in R^\times$ with $b=u z^r$, as required. The cited node is intentionally the unsplit Kato/Nizioł literature interface, not a purported smaller class-group lemma.

proof.text: If $q=0$, the original equation is $bc=1$, so take $r=0$ and $u=b$. If $P=\{0\}$ this is the only case. When $n=0$, there are no polynomial parameters and the same localization computation and recognition interface apply verbatim. No condition on perfection of the Cohen residue field has been introduced.
